questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Testing Dependency Injection”?
options: Testing Dependency Injection means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Testing Dependency Injection removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Testing Dependency Injection should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Testing Dependency Injection helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Testing Dependency Injection helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Testing Dependency Injection is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Configuring test providers” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Configuring test providers” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Configuring test providers” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Configuring test providers” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Configuring test providers” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Configuring test providers” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Configuring test providers” under Testing Dependency Injection. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Testing Dependency Injection”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
